financing.summary: Stanley Martin Homes is a private company, wholly owned by Japan's Daiwa House Industry through Daiwa House USA Holdings since February 2017. It funds itself from the parent's balance sheet: it has no public notes, no rating of its own and no disclosed credit facility, and it paid for United Homes Group (enterprise value about $221M) with cash on hand. CEO Steve Alloy calls the company land-heavy by choice. It owns and entitles hard sites itself, has an in-house land development arm (Prestige, bought in 2024), and in October 2025 sold a Prince William County tract to Amazon Data Services for about $700M. Its three 2025-2026 acquisitions bring in land-light books, though. United Homes Group controlled 96% of its roughly 7,200 lots through options, including land-bank partners and the founder's related-party developers, and it carried a $70M Kennedy Lewis term loan that Stanley Martin repaid at closing. Holiday Builders adds about 10,600 controlled Florida lots. The opening for a land banker is the parent's balance sheet. Daiwa's debt-to-equity ratio is 1.16x after hybrids (1.25x before) against a stated aim of below 1.0x by March 2027. Daiwa has also said it will balance US land investment with recovery of capital, while lifting its US forecast to 9,000 homes, with about 1,500 coming from the two 2026 acquisitions.
financing.land_strategy: Land-heavy at the core company, by its own framing. In November 2025 CEO Steve Alloy told The Builder's Daily that most national builders have sold owned land in favour of options, but Stanley Martin is not wired that way: it targets difficult sites that need complex engineering or rezoning and keeps land development and engineering staff in-house. In May 2024 Stanley Martin Holdings bought Prestige Corporate Development (land acquisition, development and lot sales, more than 8,000 lots controlled around Charlotte) and Prestige Site Works (site-development contractor). Its Integrated Report message credits growth to strategic land acquisitions and M&A, backed by Daiwa's financial strength. The acquired companies run differently. United Homes Group described itself as land-light, with 96% of about 7,200 lots under option at 31 Dec 2025. Holiday Builders bought scattered and finished lots. No owned-versus-optioned target is published for the combined company.

lots.source_title: Daiwa House FY2025 Presentation on Management Policies (May 2026), p.7: Total Land Holdings (lots) of the U.S. single-family business
lots.note: Stanley Martin's own lot count is not published. Daiwa gives one figure for its three US builders combined (Stanley Martin, Trumark, CastleRock): 75,017 lots held including controlled lots at end-December 2025, up 47% from 50,933 at end-2021, with no owned/optioned split. Stanley Martin delivered 5,320 of the group's 7,776 US homes in FY2025 (Integrated Report 2026). Known additions: Windsor Homes, about 2,100 lots (Sept 2025, already inside the Dec 2025 figure); United Homes Group, 7,225 lots at 31 Dec 2025 (284 owned, 6,941 controlled under option, so 96% optioned; UHG FY2025 10-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1830188/000183018826000009/uhg-20251231.htm); Holiday Builders, about 10,600 controlled Florida lots (Stanley Martin release, July 2026). A pro-forma Stanley Martin total cannot be built from public data.

land_banking.description: UHG's merger information statement names GSH Land Fund, LLC as a third-party land bank for United Homes Group (now a Stanley Martin subsidiary). The land purchase, option and land-banking agreements needed counterparty consents for the merger. Who owns or manages the fund is not stated.
land_banking.source_title: United Homes Group DEFM14C information statement (filed 2026-04-10)
land_banking.note: The 'GSH' prefix matches UHG's operating subsidiary Great Southern Homes, Inc. That a land bank uses the name suggests a dedicated vehicle, but its sponsor is not public (my inference). This is a lead for Domain: an existing land-bank book now inside Stanley Martin.

land_banking.counterparty: Unnamed land bank partners of United Homes Group (aggregate)
land_banking.description: UHG controlled finished lots through option contracts with third-party developers, related-party developers and land bank partners. Deposits were typically 15-20%, with staggered takedowns, and UHG usually paid development costs on land-bank deals and was reimbursed the following month. At 31 Dec 2025 lot deposits totalled $40.5M against $270.6M of remaining purchase price (6,941 option lots), down from $48.2M and $352.2M a year earlier. UHG also sold finished lots to a land banker with an option to buy them back, booked as financing at about 80% of carrying value.
land_banking.source_title: United Homes Group FY2025 10-K, Note 2 Variable Interest Entities (filed 2026-03-13)
land_banking.note: amount_usd_m is the aggregate remaining option purchase price across all option counterparties, not land-bank funding alone. Max exposure on the lot sale-repurchase financing was $0.2M at 31 Dec 2025 ($1.9M at 31 Dec 2024). Option forfeitures in 2025 were under $0.1M. Lot table and the 15-20% deposit terms are from the 10-K Item 1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1830188/000183018826000009/uhg-20251231.htm).

land_banking.counterparty: Land to Lots, LLC; PC Land Development Co., LLC; Pennington Development, LLC (Nieri-affiliated 'PC Entities')
land_banking.description: These are related-party land developers tied to UHG's controlling stockholder and former executive chairman Michael Nieri, and historically a large share of UHG's developed-lot pipeline. On 22 Feb 2026, alongside the merger agreement, UHG signed 'PC Property Agreements' with them covering Camellia Park, Palomino Oaks, Southbridge, Winter Farms and Halton Oaks. The agreements speed up UHG's purchases of lots and raw land at reduced overall contract prices. Stanley Martin knew of and approved them, and included the properties in its valuation.
land_banking.source_title: United Homes Group DEFM14C information statement (filed 2026-04-10), background of the merger and PC Property Transactions
land_banking.note: Lot counts and prices not disclosed. Related-party lot deposits were $4.9M at 31 Dec 2025 ($6.8M at 31 Dec 2024), per 10-K Note 10 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1830188/000183018826000009/R17.htm). The deal moves this land from founder-owned option supply onto the balance sheet.

land_banking.counterparty: Daiwa House Industry Co., Ltd. (through Daiwa House USA Holdings Inc.)
land_banking.description: Parent and main capital source. Daiwa House USA Holdings acquired the equity of Stanley Martin and made it a subsidiary in February 2017. The Stanley Martin CEO says growth through land acquisitions and M&A has been backed by the group's financial foundation. This is parent equity and funding, not a lot-option programme.
land_banking.source_title: Daiwa House Group Global Business: Stanley Martin (company page)
land_banking.note: CEO message in Daiwa Integrated Report 2026 (https://www.daiwahouse.com/English/ir/ar/pdf/daiwahouse_IR2026E_all.pdf, p.41). The amounts Daiwa has lent or contributed are not disclosed. Verifier 2026-11-19: the cited Daiwa page states the Feb 2017 equity acquisition (made a subsidiary) but not a 100% stake, so the description no longer says 100%.

debt.instrument: United Homes Group syndicated secured revolving line of credit (Second Amended and Restated Credit Agreement, 10 Aug 2023)
debt.rate: SOFR + 275-350 bp (7.48% weighted average at 31 Dec 2025)
debt.lenders_agent: Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. (administrative agent; Wells Fargo Securities sole lead arranger); lenders Regions Bank, Flagstar Bank, United Bank, Third Coast Bank
debt.source_title: United Homes Group 8-K filed 2026-05-04 (Item 1.02: credit agreements repaid and terminated at merger closing)
debt.note: Principal is the $220M commitment. $78.2M was drawn at 31 Dec 2025 (Wells $21.2M, Regions $17.9M, Flagstar $16.3M, United $13.0M, Third Coast $9.8M), with $56.4M available on a $136.0M borrowing base. Secured by homes under construction and developed lots. Covenant relief came through the Fourth Amendment (29 Sep 2025) and Fifth Amendment (31 Mar 2026). All loans were repaid and commitments terminated at the 4 May 2026 closing. Terms from the FY2025 10-K debt note (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1830188/000183018826000009/R16.htm). Wells Fargo and the four banks are relationship leads for Stanley Martin's Carolinas business.

debt.instrument: United Homes Group $70M subordinated term loan (Credit Agreement, 11 Dec 2024)
debt.rate: Adjusted Term SOFR + 675-775 bp (11.52% weighted average at 31 Dec 2025; 12.40% effective)
debt.lenders_agent: Kennedy Lewis Agency Partners LLC (administrative agent)
debt.note: Guaranteed by UHG and secured by a pledge of 100% of Great Southern Homes, Inc. Maturity was the earlier of 11 Dec 2030 and the revolver maturity (effectively 2 Aug 2027). It funded the redemption of $80M of convertible notes. A change of control required prepayment with the applicable premium cut by 50%, and UHG carried the embedded derivative at $4.6M at 31 Dec 2025. Carrying value $67.45M at 31 Dec 2025. Covenant relief came through the KL First Amendment (29 Sep 2025) and Second Amendment (31 Mar 2026). Repaid at the 4 May 2026 closing; payoff amount not disclosed. Terms from the 10-K debt note (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1830188/000183018826000009/R16.htm).

debt.instrument: Stanley Martin Homes / Stanley Martin Holdings bank or parent credit lines (terms not disclosed)
debt.source_title: United Homes Group DEFM14C (Parent intends to finance the merger with cash on hand; no financing condition)
debt.note: No Stanley Martin facility, lender, size or maturity is public. Stanley Martin has no SEC filings of its own. The only public statement is that it paid for UHG with cash on hand, and Daiwa describes its US builders as funded by the group. Row kept so the gap shows in the debt table.

debt.instrument: Parent-level funding: Daiwa House Industry consolidated interest-bearing liabilities (not Stanley Martin debt)
debt.rate: about 1.3% to 1.4% funding rate in Japan
debt.source_title: Daiwa House Consolidated Financial Results, first six months of FY ending March 2027 (11 Nov 2026)
debt.note: Yen figures, not converted: interest-bearing liabilities excluding leases 3,717.7 billion yen at 30 Sep 2026. Debt-to-equity 1.25x, or 1.16x counting 250 billion yen of hybrid bonds and loans at 50% equity credit. Balance-sheet lines at 30 Sep 2026: short-term bank loans 1,134.6bn, CP 255.0bn, bonds 643.0bn plus 51.0bn current, long-term bank loans 1,425.2bn plus 208.9bn current. Daiwa also has zero-coupon convertible bonds due 2029 and 2030 (conversion-price notice of 26 Jun 2026). The funding rate is from the 11 Nov 2026 analyst Q&A (Q16). How much is on-lent to Stanley Martin is not disclosed.

capital_events.description: United Homes Group (acquired by Stanley Martin in 2026) amended both credit facilities for temporary covenant relief: the Fourth Amendment to the Wells Fargo-agented revolver and the First Amendment to the Kennedy Lewis term loan.
capital_events.source_title: United Homes Group FY2025 10-K, Note 9 Debt
capital_events.note: UHG 8-K filed 2025-10-01 (Item 1.01) reports the same amendments.

capital_events.description: Land sale: Stanley Martin sold the Devlin Tech Park tract in Prince William County, VA (190 acres) to Amazon Data Services for about $700M, against roughly $51M assembled in 2021-2022. It had first rezoned the land for 516 homes, then pursued a data-centre rezoning through a two-year court fight.
capital_events.source_title: HousingWire / The Builder's Daily: Land-heavy, future-ready: Stanley Martin's $700M pivot (5 Nov 2025)
capital_events.note: Article gives $700M in the lead and $709M in an Alloy quote, and 190 acres sold out of a 270-acre assembly. Daiwa's FY2025 management-policy deck refers to a 'large-scale land transaction by the U.S. subsidiary' in FY2025 (https://www.daiwahouse.com/English/ir/challenge/pdf/FY20254Q_presentation_material_en.pdf); linking it to this sale is my inference. A large one-off cash inflow ahead of the 2026 acquisitions.

capital_events.description: Parent ratings dated 25 Mar 2026: Daiwa House Industry long-term AA- from R&I and AA from JCR. R&I short-term (CP) a-1+ dated 15 Jul 2026. Stanley Martin has no rating of its own.
capital_events.note: Integrated Report 2026 describes the R&I AA- as unchanged.

capital_events.description: UHG signed the Fifth Amendment (Wells Fargo revolver) and Second Amendment (Kennedy Lewis term loan), waiving the DSCR and leverage covenants until the Stanley Martin merger closed. If the merger missed 31 May 2026, UHG had 60 days to refinance and repay in full.
capital_events.note: UHG's final projections in the DEFM14C showed likely DSCR (1.89x and 1.99x vs 2.00x) and leverage (2.33x vs 2.25x) shortfalls in Q1-Q2 2026.

capital_events.description: At the UHG merger closing, all loans under UHG's Wells Fargo-agented revolver and Kennedy Lewis-agented term loan were repaid, commitments terminated and liens released. Stanley Martin funded the merger with cash on hand, with no financing condition.
capital_events.note: Payoff amounts not disclosed. Drawn balances at 31 Dec 2025 were $78.2M revolver and $70M term loan principal. Cash-on-hand statement from the DEFM14C.

capital_events.description: Parent guidance: after four years of heavy investment in US single-family land, Daiwa said the next three to four years will balance investment with recovery of capital. It added that US sales growth reflects continued M&A and strategic land buying.
capital_events.source_title: Daiwa House Q&A at earnings conference, FY2026 1Q (Q2, Q4, Q10, Q13)
capital_events.note: Same Q&A: debt-equity was 1.1x at end-June 2026. Holiday Builders was not in the FY2026 forecast, and goodwill amortisation will limit its profit contribution.

capital_events.description: Parent guidance: Daiwa aims to cut debt-to-equity from 1.16x (Sep 2026) to below 1.0x by March 2027, and is considering reducing interest-bearing liabilities rather than adding to them. It raised the FY2026 US single-family forecast from 8,000 to 9,000 homes, with about 1,500 from UHG and Holiday and existing operations roughly flat at 7,776.
capital_events.source_title: Daiwa House Q&A at earnings conference, FY2026 2Q (Q2, Q13, Q14)
capital_events.note: A tighter parent balance sheet alongside a bigger, more option-dependent Stanley Martin is the clearest public case for off-balance-sheet lot capital. No such arrangement has been announced.

joint_ventures.description: Coastal Loans, LLC is a mortgage joint venture between Holiday Builders (a Stanley Martin subsidiary since July 2026) and Acrisure Mortgage. Not a land JV.
joint_ventures.source_title: Holiday Builders blog: Celebrating Success - Coastal Loans (26 Feb 2025)
joint_ventures.note: Whether the JV continues after the acquisition is not stated. Stanley Martin's own mortgage and title businesses (First Heritage Mortgage, First Excel Title) are group brands, not JVs (Stanley Martin Holdings release, 13 May 2024). No land or homebuilding JV found.

key_metrics.credit_ratings: Stanley Martin: none (no rated or public debt). Parent Daiwa House Industry: R&I AA- and JCR AA long-term (25 Mar 2026); R&I a-1+ short-term (15 Jul 2026).
key_metrics.fiscal_year_end: December (Stanley Martin, per Daiwa's US reporting); parent Daiwa House fiscal year ends 31 March
key_metrics.source_title: Daiwa House IR Ratings page; Daiwa FY2026 2Q results (parent leverage 1.25x / 1.16x after hybrids)

competitor_links.relationship: Kennedy Lewis Agency Partners LLC was administrative agent and lender group lead on United Homes Group's $70M subordinated term loan (Dec 2024, SOFR + 675-775 bp). Stanley Martin repaid it and the agreement was terminated when it closed the UHG purchase on 4 May 2026. This is a credit relationship, not land banking, and no Kennedy Lewis or Millrose land-bank tie to Stanley Martin itself has been found.
competitor_links.note: Kennedy Lewis manages Millrose Properties, Domain's competitor. Kennedy Lewis therefore knew the UHG lot book until May 2026.

competitor_links.relationship: Third-party land bank for United Homes Group (now inside Stanley Martin), named in the merger information statement. Sponsor not disclosed.

ma.description: Agreement announced 16 July 2026 (Stanley Martin's website copy is dated 20 July). Holiday says the acquisition became official on 30 July 2026, and Holiday is now a wholly owned subsidiary. Price not disclosed. Holiday closed about 1,050 homes in 2025 and adds about 10,600 controlled Florida lots and 40+ communities. Zelman Partners advised Holiday, with Holland & Knight as counsel. Maynard Nexsen and Larry Eisenberg, PC acted for Stanley Martin.
ma.map_impact: Holiday (Builder 100 #62) merges into Stanley Martin (#18). Stanley Martin's Florida business grows from Orlando and Tampa to seven regional zones, from the Panhandle to the Southwest Gulf Coast. The 10,600 lots, mostly scattered and finished lots bought from developers, make Stanley Martin a much larger Florida lot buyer. Bruce Assam stays President and CEO of Holiday. Land decisions likely now involve Reston (inference).
ma.source_title: Stanley Martin Homes press release: Stanley Martin Homes to Acquire Holiday Builders (July 2026)
ma.note: Closing date from Holiday's own post of 2 Sep 2026 (https://holidaybuilders.com/holiday-builders-aquired-by-stanley-martin-homes/). The seller's adviser has reported 29 July. Daiwa lists the deal as July 2026 in its Integrated Report 2026, and its 11 Nov 2026 Q&A puts UHG plus Holiday at about 1,500 homes a year in FY2026.

ma.counterparty: United Homes Group, Inc. (Nasdaq: UHG; Great Southern Homes, Rosewood Communities)
ma.description: Merger agreement signed 22 Feb 2026 and closed 4 May 2026. All-cash, $1.18 per share, about $99.3M of equity consideration and about $221M of enterprise value. UHG became a wholly owned subsidiary, was delisted and repaid its Wells Fargo and Kennedy Lewis debt at closing. Stanley Martin's offers fell from $150M (June 2025) to $94M (Nov 2025) before the final $99.3M, and rival bids (Parties A, C, F) fell away. Vestra Advisors and Paul, Weiss advised UHG's special committee, with Maynard Nexsen for Stanley Martin.
ma.map_impact: UHG (Builder 100 #56, 1,192 closings in 2025) merges into Stanley Martin. It adds Columbia/Midlands, Upstate (Greenville-Spartanburg-Clemson), Coastal/Myrtle Beach, Augusta GA, Raleigh and the Rosewood move-up brand, plus 7,225 lots that were 96% optioned. Stanley Martin has since opened Florence SC and branded Myrtle Beach. UHG's executive officers (Jack Micenko, Keith Feldman, Michael Nieri, Tom O'Grady, Robert Penny, Jeremy Pyle, Shelton Twine) left at closing. The related-party Nieri lot pipeline was reset by the PC Property Agreements.
ma.source_title: United Homes Group 8-K filed 2026-05-04 (completion of merger with Stanley Martin Homes)
ma.note: Enterprise value and 1,192 closings from Stanley Martin's release (https://www.stanleymartin.com/blog/448/stanley-martin-homes-completes-acquisition-of-united-homes-group). Bid history and the $99,325,000 figure from the DEFM14C (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1830188/000114036126014128/ny20067664x2_defm14c.htm). Myrtle Beach entry via Great Southern Homes per Stanley Martin release of Sep 2026 (https://www.stanleymartin.com/blog/455/stanley-martin-homes-expands-coastal-carolina-presence-with-entry-into-myrtle-beach-market).

ma.counterparty: Windsor Homes (Windsor Investments, LLC and affiliates), Greensboro, NC
ma.description: Announced 17 Sep 2025. Stanley Martin bought the assets and operations (land, homes, staff) and closed on 25 Sep 2025 US time. Windsor delivered 334 homes in 2024, controlled about 2,100 lots in the Triad (Greensboro, Winston-Salem, High Point, Burlington) and Wilmington, and had 270 homes under construction. Price not disclosed; Daiwa says no significant impact on results. Whelan Advisory advised Windsor (counsel Williams Parker), with Maynard Nexsen for Stanley Martin.
ma.map_impact: Adds the North Carolina Triad and Wilmington, 32 communities and roughly 25% more controlled lots in North Carolina. Tom Hall was Windsor's president. Not a ranked builder, so no Builder 100 row merges.
ma.source_title: Daiwa House press release: Stanley Martin Homes Has Acquired the Homebuilding Business of Windsor Homes (26 Sep 2025)
ma.note: Announcement details from Stanley Martin's release (https://www.stanleymartin.com/blog/429/stanley-martin-homes-to-acquire-the-assets-and-operations-of-windsor-homes-expanding-presence-in-north-carolina).

ma.counterparty: Prestige Corporate Development and Prestige Site Works (Charlotte, NC metro)
ma.description: Context, pre-2025. Stanley Martin Holdings agreed to buy a land acquisition, development and lot-sales business that controlled more than 8,000 Charlotte-area lots, plus a site-development contractor working on 15 projects (more than 2,500 lots) in North and South Carolina. Closing was expected in May 2024. Owner Brian Mahoney; Prestige president Steve Bailey.
ma.map_impact: Gives Stanley Martin an in-house lot developer and lot seller in Charlotte, so it is both a land buyer and a potential lot supplier to other builders, and a possible counterparty for land-bank structures. Daiwa lists Prestige as a wholly owned subsidiary from 2024.
ma.source_title: Stanley Martin Holdings press release: Acquires Prestige Corporate Development and Prestige Site Works (13 May 2024)
ma.note: Included for land-map context although before 2025. Closing confirmed by Daiwa's Stanley Martin page ('made Prestige Corporate Development, LLC into a wholly owned subsidiary in 2024').

gaps: Stanley Martin credit facility (size, agent bank, lenders, maturity): not publicly disclosed (private Daiwa subsidiary, no SEC filings of its own).
Senior notes or other public debt: none found; Stanley Martin issues no public securities. Funding appears to come through Daiwa House, but intercompany loan or guarantee amounts are not disclosed.

Owned versus optioned lots, total lots controlled and years of supply for Stanley Martin: not publicly disclosed. Daiwa publishes only 75,017 lots for its three US builders combined (Dec 2025). A pro-forma Stanley Martin total including UHG (7,225) and Holiday (~10,600) cannot be built.
Cash, total debt, liquidity and leverage for Stanley Martin: not publicly disclosed.

Land-banking or lot-option partners of the Stanley Martin core business: none publicly named. No public link found to Domain Real Estate Partners, Millrose, TPG Angelo Gordon, DW Partners, Essential Housing, IHP Capital, Brookfield, Varde, Oaktree, GTIS, Hearthstone, Walton or Forestar. One combined web search returned nothing; per-firm searches were not run.
GSH Land Fund, LLC (UHG's land bank): sponsor, size and lot count not disclosed.
Whether UHG's land-bank and related-party option contracts continued unchanged after closing, and whether Stanley Martin funded any of them onto its balance sheet: not publicly disclosed.
UHG debt payoff amounts at closing (revolver balance, Kennedy Lewis prepayment premium): not disclosed in the closing 8-K.
Holiday Builders and Windsor Homes purchase prices, and whether Holiday debt was assumed or repaid: not publicly disclosed.
Daiwa House's own release on the UHG and Holiday deals was not found on its English release index (only the Windsor and CRC Holdings notices were located), so Daiwa-side deal terms are not shown.
Devlin Tech Park sale: secondary source only (trade press). No county deed or Stanley Martin / Daiwa release was opened, and the $700M versus $709M figure is unresolved.
